$comment: Single source of truth for research references cited in user-facing templates and tabs (Appeal Letter, Detector Literacy, Risk Profiler, About). scripts/check-references.mjs and the Rust test in src-tauri/src/appeal_letter.rs verify that every reference key used in user-facing text exists here. Add new references ONLY with a DOI that has been fetched and verified; record the verification in docs/DECISIONS.md.

liang-2023.full_citation: Liang, W., Yuksekgonul, M., Mao, Y., Wu, E., & Zou, J. (2023). GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. Patterns, 4(7), 100779. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2023.100779
liang-2023.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
liang-2023.used_for: Evidence that AI-text detectors can misclassify non-native English writing; motivates the caution shown by the Risk Profile and Appeal Letter features.

weber-wulff-2023.full_citation: Weber-Wulff, D., Anohina-Naumeca, A., Bjelobaba, S., Foltýnek, T., Guerrero-Dib, J., Popoola, O., Šigut, P., & Waddington, L. (2023). Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text. International Journal for Educational Integrity, 19(1), 26. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40979-023-00146-z
weber-wulff-2023.title: Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text
weber-wulff-2023.used_for: Independent evaluation of 14 AI-text detection tools: the study concludes the tools are neither accurate nor reliable and tend to label text as human-written, with both false positives and false negatives observed. ScholarScribe must not claim that all tools showed high false-positive rates.

laban-2024.reason: Cited in v2.2.1 as 'Laban et al. (2024), Determining the believability and harm of AI-generated outputs, ACL 2024'. No such paper could be identified on 2026-10-13 via Crossref queries by title and author (api.crossref.org). The closest real Laban et al. 2024 work is 'Can LLM-Generated Misinformation Be Detected?' (ICLR 2024), which studies detection of LLM-generated misinformation, not the accuracy of AI-text detectors, and therefore does not support the detector-literacy claims it was cited for. Removed everywhere (README, USER_MANUAL, Detector Literacy tab) per milestone task T1.3. Do not re-add without a verified DOI.

weber-wulff-2023-patterns-100846.reason: An incorrect bibliographic identity that circulated in v2.2.1 ('Testing of detection signals for AI-generated text', Patterns, DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100846). Crossref shows that DOI belongs to 'Revealing factors influencing polymer degradation with rank-based machine learning' (Yuan et al., Patterns 2023), which is unrelated. Replaced everywhere by the verified weber-wulff-2023 entry above.
